summary:
Grixistax (October 2026) is a Kraum + Tevesh Szat partner prison deck: Contamination, Blood Moon, Back to Basics, Trinisphere and Chalice, with artifact mana to break parity. Tevesh's Thrulls pay for everything. This review re-verifies the eighteen items of the deck's rules attestation, and confirms the Helm of Obedience and Breach lines against cached Commander Spellbook steps.

Rules surprise: Blood Moon switches off the deck's own Phyrexian Tower and other utility lands (anti-synergy flag, no list change).

interactions.title: Partners: Kraum + Tevesh Szat
interactions.ruling: Both have partner, so they can be co-commanders; combined identity is blue, black and red. Either one satisfies 'if you control a commander' (Fierce Guardianship, Deflecting Swat, Deadly Rollick). Commander tax is tracked separately for each. Mox Amber makes one mana of a color among your legendary creatures and planeswalkers: Kraum gives blue or red, Tevesh gives black.

rulings.quote: An effect that checks whether you control your commander is satisfied if you control one or both of your two commanders.
Mox Amber's ability adds one mana of the color of your choice from among the colors of legendary creatures and legendary planeswalkers you control. It doesn't add one mana of each of those colors.

source.item: Partner commanders and combined color identity
Commander-dependent free spells and Mox Amber

interactions.title: Kraum: once per opponent per turn, under Damping Sphere too
interactions.ruling: Kraum draws when one opponent casts their second spell in a turn. It's once per opponent per turn, two spells from different opponents don't count, and it looks at the whole turn even if Kraum arrived late. Damping Sphere taxes each extra spell but doesn't forbid it, so an opponent who pays still gives you a card.

rulings.quote: One opponent must cast two spells for Kraum's triggered ability to trigger. Two spells from different opponents won't cause it to trigger.
Kraum's triggered ability can trigger only once each turn for each opponent.
Damping Sphere’s second ability counts spells that were cast during a turn even if Damping Sphere wasn’t on the battlefield as they were cast.

source.item: Damping Sphere and Kraum's second-spell trigger

interactions.title: Tevesh Thrulls feed every sacrifice outlet
interactions.ruling: Tevesh's +2 makes two 0/1 Thrulls. They pay Contamination's upkeep, die at once to Skullclamp (+1/-1 makes them 1/0, a state-based death, draw two), and are sacrifice fodder for Phyrexian Tower ({B}{B}), Culling the Weak ({B}{B}{B}{B}) and Diabolic Intent. Tevesh's +1 can also sacrifice one to draw two (three if it was a commander). You choose what to sacrifice as the ability resolves.
interactions.short: 0/1 Thrulls: Contamination upkeep, Skullclamp draws, Tower/Culling mana, Diabolic Intent.

oracle.quote: +2: Create two 0/1 black Thrull creature tokens.
Whenever equipped creature dies, draw two cards.

rulings.quote: For the second ability of Tevesh Szat, Doom of Fools, you choose whether to sacrifice anything and what to sacrifice as the ability resolves.

source.item: Tevesh Szat plus Phyrexian Tower / Culling the Weak / Diabolic Intent

interactions.title: Contamination, Damping Sphere and Blood Moon on the same land
interactions.ruling: Contamination makes every land produce exactly {B}. Damping Sphere turns a land that would make two or more into {C}. When both apply to one tap, the land's controller picks which applies first, and either way Ancient Tomb gives one mana. Blood Moon makes nonbasics Mountains ({T}: Add {R}), and Contamination still turns that into {B}. Artifact mana is untouched by all three.
interactions.short: Lands make one {B} under Contamination; artifact mana is the parity breaker.

oracle.quote: If a land is tapped for mana, it produces {B} instead of any other type and amount.
If a land is tapped for two or more mana, it produces {C} instead of any other type and amount.

rulings.quote: If multiple replacement effects would modify the mana an ability you control produces, choose one to apply. After that, determine if any others are applicable.
The second ability of this card is a replacement effect, not a triggered ability.

source.item: Contamination with Blood Moon and artifact mana

interactions.title: Blood Moon strips your own utility lands; Back to Basics still locks them
interactions.ruling: Blood Moon makes nonbasic lands Mountains: they lose every other ability, enters-tapped clauses included. Your Phyrexian Tower stops being a sacrifice outlet, and fetchlands and Ancient Tomb stop working. They remain nonbasic (Blood Moon doesn't change supertypes or names), so Back to Basics still keeps them from untapping. That locks your own nonbasics as hard as your opponents'.
interactions.short: Under Blood Moon, Phyrexian Tower is just a Mountain; Back to Basics still stops it untapping.

flag.note: Accepted prison cost, documented by the source for Back to Basics. The extra point here is that Blood Moon switches off the deck's own Phyrexian Tower (the Thrull mana outlet). Sequence Tower activations before Moon. No list change.

oracle.quote: Nonbasic lands don't untap during their controllers' untap steps.

rulings.quote: This effect doesn't affect names or supertypes. It won't turn any land into a basic land or remove the legendary supertype from a legendary land, and the lands won't be named "Mountain."
Nonbasic lands will lose any other land types and abilities they had. They will gain the land type Mountain and gain the ability "{T}: Add {R}."

source.item: Blood Moon plus Back to Basics

interactions.title: Overburden and Tangle Wire with Thrull tokens
interactions.ruling: Overburden only triggers on nontoken creatures, so Thrulls are free; casting Kraum bounces one of your lands. At your upkeep, Tangle Wire's fading trigger and tap trigger are both yours to order. Resolve fading first so the tap trigger counts one fewer counter. Untapped Thrulls can be the permanents you tap.

oracle.quote: Whenever a player puts a nontoken creature onto the battlefield, that player returns a land they control to its owner's hand.
At the beginning of each player's upkeep, that player taps an untapped artifact, creature, or land they control for each fade counter on this artifact.

interactions.title: Trinisphere and Chalice tax your own free spells
interactions.ruling: An untapped Trinisphere applies after alternative costs and reductions. Force of Will's pitch, a free Fierce Guardianship or Pact, and 0-cost artifacts all cost three mana. Chalice checks mana value as the spell is cast, not what was paid. At 0 it counters your Moxen, LED and Lotus Petal; at 1 it counters your Sol Ring, Vampiric Tutor and similar.
interactions.short: Trinisphere makes free spells cost 3; Chalice at 0 or 1 hits your own fast mana.

oracle.quote: As long as this artifact is untapped, each spell that would cost less than three mana to cast costs three mana to cast.
Whenever a player casts a spell with mana value equal to the number of charge counters on this artifact, counter that spell.

rulings.quote: Finally, apply Trinisphere's effect if the mana component of the spell's cost is less than three mana.
If there are zero charge counters on Chalice of the Void, it counters each spell with a mana value of 0.

interactions.title: Karn locks the Wishclaw you hand over
interactions.ruling: After Wishclaw's tutor resolves, an opponent gains control of it. With Karn out, opponents can't activate abilities of artifacts they control, so they can't use it. Karn doesn't stop triggered abilities. His -2 needs an artifact you own from outside the game or face-up in exile; the deck doesn't plan on a wishboard.

oracle.quote: Activated abilities of artifacts your opponents control can't be activated.

rulings.quote: Triggered abilities (starting with "when," "whenever," or "at") are unaffected by Karn.

source.item: Karn, the Great Creator plus Wishclaw Talisman

interactions.title: Helm of Obedience + Leyline of the Void or Dauthi Voidwalker
interactions.ruling: With Leyline or Voidwalker exiling cards that would go to the opponent's graveyard, Helm's mill never puts a card there. The stop condition is never met, so X = 1 exiles the opponent's whole library. Voidwalker's exiled cards also get void counters.
interactions.short: Helm for {1} + graveyard hate = exile an opponent's entire library.

rulings.quote: If an effect like that of Leyline of the Void prevents cards from being put into your opponent’s graveyard, the process described in the first sentence of Helm of Obedience’s effect will never stop. Your opponent’s entire library will be exiled, even if X is 1.

spellbook.quote: Activate Helm of Obedience by paying {1} and tapping it, causing target opponent to mill a card.
Due to Dauthi Voidwalker's replacement effect, the milled card is exiled instead of going to the graveyard, and that opponents repeats that process until their library is empty.

source.item: Helm of Obedience plus Leyline of the Void or Dauthi Voidwalker

interactions.title: The Breach finish needs your own prison pieces gone
interactions.ruling: Breach + LED + Brain Freeze needs six other cards in hand and/or graveyard. Under your own Trinisphere, every escaped LED costs three mana. Damping Sphere taxes each successive spell. Chalice on 0 counters LED, and Contamination turns lands black-only. Necropotence exiles discarded cards (LED's discard), cutting Breach fuel. Remove or sequence around these before going off.

oracle.quote: Whenever you discard a card, exile that card from your graveyard.

spellbook.quote: You have at least six other cards in hand and/or graveyard.
Cast Lion's Eye Diamond from your graveyard for its escape cost by exiling three cards besides Brain Freeze from your graveyard.

source.item: Underworld Breach plus Lion's Eye Diamond plus Brain Freeze
Necropotence with commander draw and Breach

interactions.title: Tainted Pact as a tutor, and Tevesh's −10
interactions.ruling: The list has 100 distinct names, two partners included, so Tainted Pact never stops on a duplicate; it's a tutor here, since there's no Thassa's Oracle. Tevesh's −10 takes control of every commander on the battlefield first, then puts all commanders from command zones onto the battlefield under your control. If you leave the game, the ones you put onto the battlefield are exiled.

oracle.quote: −10: Gain control of all commanders. Put all commanders from the command zone onto the battlefield under your control.

rulings.quote: As the third ability is resolving, you'll gain control of all commanders that were already on the battlefield before the commanders from the command zone enter the battlefield under your control.
